papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section 2 overview and section 5 conclusions.
papers.what_it_is: A Perspective article on quantum sensor technologies (atom interferometry, clocks, optomechanics) for particle physics experiments.
papers.why_not: The paper concerns quantum sensing hardware for particle physics. It has no quantum computing, machine learning, finance or evaluation-method content.

papers.title_in_file: Fast gradient estimation for variational quantum algorithms
papers.what_it_is: A Bayesian method, built on the generalized parameter shift rule, for estimating gradients of variational quantum algorithms with fewer measurement rounds.

assertions.value: The authors report that their Bayesian gradient estimation reduces the required measurement rounds by up to an order of magnitude for a common QAOA setup.
quotes: reducing the required measurement rounds by up to an order of magnitude for a common QAOA setup
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result in the paper for one QAOA setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The size of the gain is specific to the tested QAOA setup and may not carry to other circuits.

assertions.value: The authors state that their analysis neglects all error sources from imperfect quantum hardware and covers only noise from finite measurements (shot noise).
quotes: we neglect all error sources arising from imperfect quantum hardware and only focus on noise due to finite measurements (i.e. shot noise)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own analysis scope, Introduction, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors report that estimation via finite differences can outperform the parameter shift rule in gradient accuracy for small and moderate measurement budgets.
quotes: an estimation via finite differences can outperform the parameter shift rule in terms of gradient accuracy for small and moderate measurement budgets
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from the paper's own simulations.

papers.title_in_file: PAC-learning of free-fermionic states is NP-hard
papers.what_it_is: A computational complexity result: deciding whether a dataset of Majorana correlation estimates is consistent with a free-fermionic state is NP-complete, which makes proper PAC-learning of such states NP-hard.

assertions.value: The paper proves that deciding whether a dataset of a few Majorana correlation function estimates can be consistent with a free-fermionic state is an NP-complete problem.
quotes: We establish that deciding whether a given dataset, formed by a few Majorana correlation functions estimates, can be consistent with a free-fermionic state is an NP-complete problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 (NP-completeness of Gaussian Consistency), Section 1.2.

assertions.value: The paper states that its results directly imply that free-fermionic states are computationally hard to properly PAC-learn.
quotes: our results directly imply that free-fermionic states are computationally hard to properly PAC-learn
assertions.certainty_reason: Corollary 1, Section 1.2, derived from Theorem 1.

assertions.value: The authors state that they have shown proper PAC-learning is hard for Majorana expectation values, and that this does not necessarily extend to improper PAC-learning.
quotes: We have shown that proper PAC-learning is hard with respect Majorana expectation values, however this does not necessarily extend to the realm of improper PAC-learning
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit of their own result, Section 1.3.

papers.title_in_file: Error Analysis of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver Algorithm
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of how Pauli errors affect convergence of the variational quantum eigensolver on small hydrogen molecule problems.

assertions.value: The authors report, from explicit simulation, that the VQE algorithm effectively collapses already when single errors occur during a quantum processing call.
quotes: we show through explicit simulation that the VQE algorithm effectively collapses already when single errors occur during a quantum processing call
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The result rests on simulation of a specific ansatz and error model, not on hardware runs.

assertions.value: The authors report that for a VQE computation requiring a six-qubit ansatz circuit with 20 layers, an error rate of less than 0.18% is required and less than 1% of ansatz circuit computations may be erroneous, otherwise errors deny convergence to the optimum.
quotes: For a VQE computation requiring a six-qubit ansatz circuit with 20 layers, an error rate of less than 0.18% is required and less than 1% of ansatz circuit computations may be erroneous, otherwise errors deny convergence to the optimum.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result for one ansatz size.

assertions.value: The authors state that they investigated H2 and chains of four hydrogen atoms, and that they ran an exhaustive Pauli error simulation of the ansatz circuits.
assertions.anchor: Section III and Section V (simulation setup)
quotes: Molecules consisting of H2 or chains of four hydrogen atoms were investigated.
an exhaustive Pauli error simulation was performed, i.e. each Pauli X, Z, Y error at each possible error location in the ansatz circuit was simulated
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own simulation setup and scope.

papers.title_in_file: Adaptive Learning for Quantum Linear Regression
papers.what_it_is: An adaptive precision-vector encoding for linear regression as a QUBO problem, tested on synthetic datasets with simulated and D-Wave quantum annealing and classical solvers.

assertions.value: The authors report that their adaptive formulation delivers improved solution quality in all instances.
quotes: The results show that our formulation is able to deliver improved solution quality in all instances
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on synthetic data.

assertions.value: The authors state that the solution quality of the optimization is limited by currently available quantum devices, which struggle to embed the necessary precision.
quotes: However, the solution quality of the optimization is limited by currently available quantum devices, which struggle to embed the necessary precision.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit in Section IV.

assertions.value: The authors state that the approach is evaluated on synthetic datasets of increasing size.
quotes: This approach is evaluated on synthetic datasets of increasing size
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own evaluation scope in the abstract.

papers.what_it_is: A hybrid quantum-classical Fourier-regression method for hyperparameter search, tested on a proprietary airline no-show dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that, for a Ridge model, their method saved 73% of the experimentation time compared with classical Grid Search with cross-validation, which took 2075 seconds.
quotes: Here we are saving 73% of the experimentation time.
the model retraining took about 5 seconds compared to 2075 seconds to get the same parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-experiment result from the authors, with a proprietary dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that for databases generated classically in less than one minute it is not worth using their algorithm.
quotes: We have realized that for databases classically generated for less than one minute, it is not worth using our algorithm
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state a limit of their own method in Section VI.

assertions.value: The authors state that the data used is a proprietary Vueling no-show dataset.
quotes: The data used in this work is a proprietary Vueling no-show dataset
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own data setup in Section II.
assertions.reader_inference: The dataset is not public, so the results cannot be reproduced from the paper alone.

assertions.value: The authors claim that their approach outperforms traditional hyperparameter optimization methods in accuracy and convergence speed for the given search space.
quotes: The results show that our approach outperforms traditional hyperparameter optimization methods in terms of accuracy and convergence speed for the given search space.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract claim by the authors.

papers.title_in_file: Assessing projected quantum kernels for the classification of IoT data
papers.what_it_is: An empirical comparison of projected quantum kernels, standard quantum kernels and classical methods on an IoT office-occupancy dataset, using a noiseless simulator.

assertions.value: The authors report that the projected quantum kernel demonstrates comparable effectiveness to classical methods when the proposed shallow circuit is used for quantum encoding.
quotes: Our findings show that the PQK demonstrates comparable effectiveness to classical methods when the proposed shallow circuit is used for quantum encoding.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on one dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that projected quantum kernels provide a moderate but statistically significant advantage over standard quantum kernels in accuracy and F1 scores.
quotes: PQKs provide a moderate but statistically significant advantage over QKs in terms of quantitative metrics (accuracy and F1 scores)
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on one dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that their findings are based on a single dataset collected from a specific office environment.
quotes: It is important to note that the findings of this study are based on a single dataset collected from a specific office environment.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit in Section 6.

assertions.value: The authors state that their analysis employs a noiseless simulator and that the next step is real noisy hardware.
quotes: our current analysis employs a noiseless simulator, which is adequate for initial tests on shallow circuits and shot noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own simulator setup in Section 6.

papers.title_in_file: Loading Probability Distributions in a Quantum circuit
papers.what_it_is: A method to build parameterized quantum circuits, tuned by a variational solver, that load symmetric and asymmetric probability distributions, tested on simulators and IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that the circuits they propose perform well when compared with the Ry-CZ circuits.
quotes: Although, the circuits proposed here performs well when compared with the Ry-CZ circuits
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own comparison, Section 5.

assertions.value: The authors report that the Gaussian distribution generated on quantum hardware is quite close to the expected one, but that they see some deficiencies in the log-normal distribution generated on hardware.
quotes: The Gaussian distribution generated by the quantum hardware is quite close to the expected distribution.
However, we do see some deficiencies in the log-normal distribution as generated by the quantum hardware.
assertions.certainty_reason: Hardware result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the proposed circuits require some qubit connectivity that may not be readily available in the hardware, and that error mitigation methods will be needed to yield accurate results.
quotes: The circuits proposed here requires some amount of connectivity between the qubits, which may not be readily available in the hardwares.
We will need error mitigation methods in our sampler to yield accurate results.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state limits of their method in Section 5.
